extension.summary: Vintage Radar (OpenGL) for 32-bit Android Kodi: Fire TV, many Google TV boxes, Chromecast with Google TV
extension.description: The same green-phosphor radar scope as "Vintage Radar (OpenGL)", built for 32-bit Android (armeabi-v7a). Install this one if your Android or Google TV Kodi is a 32-bit app, which is the case on many Fire TV and Google TV boxes; install "Vintage Radar (OpenGL, macOS and 64-bit Android)" on 64-bit Android and macOS. It shows the aircraft actually overhead, fetched live from adsb.lol with OpenSky as a fallback, centred on the place you choose and scaled to the range you choose. Every contact is dead-reckoned between updates, so blips glide instead of jumping, and past sweep echoes stay on the glass. The right side carries a nearest-first contact list and a spotlight card that rotates through the contacts showing everything the transponder reports: hex, registration, type, squawk, category, vertical rate, track, IAS/TAS/Mach, position, navigation settings, signal quality and service flags. Four phosphors, CRT scanlines and vignette, dimming, and display detail for slow boxes. The graphics are drawn with OpenGL, so the sweep stays smooth at full screen. Data: adsb.lol and the OpenSky Network; no account or key needed.
extension.disclaimer: This is a native add-on: it is built per platform and Kodi version (this one: Kodi 21 Omega, 32-bit ARM Android). Aircraft data comes from the volunteer-run adsb.lol and OpenSky Network APIs and is used as-is; it is not for navigation or flight safety. The typeface is Doto (SIL Open Font License 1.1), baked into texture atlases under resources/media/fonts.
